voci.titolo: Bessent’s Bond Gains Wiped Out as Treasury Yields Jump Again
voci.riassunto: The yields on the longest-dated US government bonds shot back to levels seen just before Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent shocked markets last month by expanding a buyback program in an effort to halt the rise.

voci.titolo: Vanguard, BlackRock ETF Shuffle Lets Foreign Investors Duck US Tax
voci.riassunto: Major institutions are flipping between near-identical equity funds to avoid receiving dividends — and the 30% tax that comes with them.

voci.titolo: First Eagle Investments' Appio on Bond Market Selloff
voci.riassunto: First Eagle Investments' Idanna Appio discusses the ongoing rise in bond yields and the broad selloff across global fixed income markets. Appio says the move is not just a US story, but a global one driven by several factors. She speaks with David Ingles and Yvonne Man on August 1, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

voci.titolo: This could be the 10-year Treasury’s tipping point into the danger zone
voci.riassunto: An unrelenting rout has global bond yields touching their highest levels since 2008, driving up borrowing costs for households, businesses and world governments.

voci.titolo: Bond Traders Snap Up Protection Against Soaring Treasury Yields
voci.riassunto: Traders are scrambling to shield their portfolios against further losses in Treasuries, as worries over the budget deficit and inflation push yields toward multiyear highs.

voci.titolo: Euro zone inflation is back above 3%. Higher interest rates are likely to follow
voci.riassunto: The European Central Bank is seen hiking rates in September as the Iran war raises energy costs in the region.

voci.titolo: Bond Slide Spreads to Emerging Markets on Fed Rate Hike Bets
voci.riassunto: A global bond selloff spread to emerging markets as investors dumped the riskier debt on expectations that the Federal Reserve will increase US interest rates later this month.

voci.titolo: Gold Approaches Two-Week Low on Rising Yields, Fed Hike Bets
voci.riassunto: Gold fell to the lowest in almost two weeks as a global bond selloff sent yields higher, with traders betting the Federal Reserve may need to raise interest rates to contain inflationary pressure from elevated oil prices.

voci.titolo: Stocks, Bonds Fall as Oil Jumps on US-Iran Jitters: Markets Wrap
voci.riassunto: A surge in oil prices rippled through global markets, hitting stocks and bonds on worries that higher energy costs will fuel inflation and force the Federal Reserve to boost rates.

voci.titolo: Bank of England chief warns new AI models threaten global financial stability
voci.riassunto: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey has warned that frontier AI could materially increase cyber risks to the global financial system.

voci.titolo: India’s economy expands 7.8% in fiscal first quarter, beating estimates
voci.riassunto: The economy was driven by a strong performance in the financial, real estate, information technology and professional services sectors.

voci.titolo: China's factory activity shrinks for second straight month, contracting less than expected
voci.riassunto: China's manufacturing activity shrank for a second straight month, keeping pressure on Beijing to support the economy as growth loses momentum.

voci.titolo: Singapore tackles finances and culture to avert a demographic crisis
voci.riassunto: One challenge for policy makers is that success on many measures won't show up immediately.

voci.titolo: K, C or E? Why economists can’t agree on the shape of today’s economy
voci.riassunto: Economists have long viewed the post-pandemic economy as "K"-shaped. That consensus has now evaporated.

voci.titolo: Fed Chairman Warsh expresses concern about inflation, advocates for 'quieter' central bank
voci.riassunto: He used the speech to outline his philosophy on policymaking while carefully sidestepping any signals

voci.titolo: Fed's Hammack says 'now is the time to act' on raising interest rates
voci.riassunto: She still thinks the Fed needs to take action against inflation that is straining household budgets.

voci.titolo: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge shows core prices rose 3.3% annually in July
voci.riassunto: The personal consumption expenditures price index was expected to rise 0.1% monthly and 3.6% on a 12-month basis, according to economists surveyed by Dow Jones.

voci.titolo: Stanley Druckenmiller leads doubters who think Bessent's bond ploys will fail
voci.riassunto: The bond market interventions have generated a modest decline in yields along with a growing chorus of derision.
